title: Go-Browse: Training Web Agents with Structured Exploration
claim: Exploration is a nested loop: an outer loop grows a page frontier while an inner loop proposes, filters, and samples tasks.
layout: 2 columns: outer-loop iterations left, three stacked inner-loop stages right; top-to-bottom flow
description: The figure has two halves. On the left, the Outer Loop (global website coverage) is drawn as three iterations separated by dashed lines. It starts with a lone Dashboard page and grows into a graph of page nodes: Products, Best Sellers, then Quest Lumaflex. Edges are curved arrows with dots, and the purple dashed 'Update Frontier' arrow marks newly discovered pages. On the right, the Inner Loop (local webpage exploration) is a curly bracket opening onto three tinted horizontal bands. The first band, blue, is Propose Tasks and shows an explorer icon and a speech bubble with example tasks. The second band, pink, is Check Feasibility and shows a robot checker, red failed paths marked with X, and a green path with a check mark. The third band, yellow, is Sample Trajectories and shows solver robots and highlighted trajectories. Dashed arrows link the bands.
caption: Overview of the \gobrowse algorithm for web agent data collection for a website. \gobrowse's outer-loop (left) maintains an exploration frontier of discovered but not yet fully explored webpages. \gobrowse's inner loop (right) explores each webpage in the frontier by (1) Proposing tasks for that webpage that are grounded in interaction; (2) Checking the feasibility of those tasks; and (3) Sampling trajectories and discovering new webpages by solving feasible tasks.\vspace{-5mm}
abstract: One of the fundamental problems in digital agents is their lack of understanding of their environment. For instance, a web browsing agent may get lost in unfamiliar websites, uncertain what pages must be visited to achieve its goals. To address this, we propose Go-Browse, a method for automatically collecting diverse and realistic web agent data at scale through structured exploration of web environments. Go-Browse achieves efficient exploration by framing data collection as a graph search, enabling reuse of information across exploration episodes. We instantiate our method on the WebArena benchmark, collecting a dataset of 10K successful task-solving trajectories and 40K interaction steps across 100 URLs. Fine-tuning a 7B parameter language model on this dataset achieves a success rate of 21.7% on the WebArena benchmark, beating GPT-4o mini by 2.4% and exceeding current state-of-the-art results for sub-10B parameter models by 2.9%.
